content: Calcium carbonate can increase gastric pH, which may interfere with the absorption and effectiveness of various medications. Below are detailed interactions and recommendations for co-administration: 1. Elvitegravir/Cobicistat/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir DF: Calcium carbonate reduces the levels of this combination by inhibiting gastrointestinal (GI) absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Separate administration by at least 2 hours. Use caution and monitor closely. 2. Enalapril: Calcium carbonate decreases the effects of enalapril through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. 3. Ephedrine: Calcium carbonate increases the levels or effects of ephedrine by enhancing passive renal tubular reabsorption in a basic urine environment. Use caution and monitor closely. 4. Erythromycin (Base, Ethylsuccinate, Lactobionate, Stearate): Calcium carbonate increases the levels of erythromycin by an unknown mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. 5. Esmolol: Calcium carbonate decreases the effects and levels of esmolol by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Separate administration by 2 hours. Use caution and monitor closely. 6. Estramustine: Calcium carbonate reduces the levels of estramustine by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Patients should take estramustine with water at least 1 hour before or 2 hours after meals. Use caution and monitor closely. 7. Etidronate: Calcium carbonate decreases the levels of etidronate by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Separate administration by 30 minutes. Use caution and monitor closely. 8. Felodipine: Calcium carbonate reduces the effects of felodipine through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely. 9. Ferric Maltol, Ferrous Fumarate, Ferrous Gluconate: Calcium carbonate decreases the levels or effects of these iron supplements by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 10. Flecainide: Calcium carbonate increases the levels or effects of flecainide by enhancing passive renal tubular reabsorption in a basic urine environment. Use caution and monitor closely. 11. Fosamprenavir: Calcium carbonate decreases the levels or effects of fosamprenavir by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 12. Fosinopril: Calcium carbonate reduces the effects of fosinopril through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. 13. Gabapentin and Gabapentin Enacarbil: Calcium carbonate decreases the levels of these agents by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Separate administration by 2 hours. Use caution and monitor closely. 14. Gefitinib: Calcium carbonate decreases the levels of gefitinib by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Separate gefitinib and antacid doses by at least 6 hours. Use caution and monitor closely. 15. Gemifloxacin: Calcium carbonate and gemifloxacin can mutually decrease each other's levels by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Separate administration by 2 hours. Use caution and monitor closely. 16. Glipizide and Glyburide: Calcium carbonate increases the levels or effects of these antidiabetic agents by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 17. Ibandronate: Calcium carbonate decreases the levels of ibandronate by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Separate administration by 30 minutes. Use caution and monitor closely. 18. Isoniazid: Calcium carbonate decreases the levels of isoniazid by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Separate administration by 2 hours. Use caution and monitor closely. 19. Itraconazole and Ketoconazole: Calcium carbonate decreases the levels of these antifungal agents by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Administer acid-neutralizing medicines at least 2 hours before or after itraconazole or ketoconazole. Use caution and monitor closely. 20. Labetalol: Calcium carbonate decreases the effects and levels of labetalol by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Separate administration by 2 hours. Use caution and monitor closely. 21. Lactulose: Calcium carbonate reduces the effects of lactulose through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor closely. 22. Lanthanum Carbonate: Calcium carbonate interacts via cation binding in the GI tract. Administer antacids at least 2 hours before or after lanthanum. Use caution and monitor closely. 23. Ledipasvir/Sofosbuvir: Calcium carbonate decreases the levels of ledipasvir due to reduced solubility at higher pH levels. Separate antacid and ledipasvir/sofosbuvir administration by 4 hours. Use caution and monitor closely. 24. Levofloxacin: Calcium carbonate and levofloxacin can mutually decrease each other's levels by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Separate administration by 2 hours. Use caution and monitor closely. 25. Levothyroxine: Calcium carbonate decreases the levels of levothyroxine by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Separate administration by 4 hours. Use caution and monitor closely. 26. Lisdexamfetamine: Calcium carbonate increases the levels or effects of lisdexamfetamine by enhancing passive renal tubular reabsorption in a basic urine environment. Use caution and monitor closely. 27. Memantine: Calcium carbonate increases the levels or effects of memantine by enhancing passive renal tubular reabsorption in a basic urine environment. Use caution and monitor closely. 28. Methscopolamine: Calcium carbonate decreases the levels of methscopolamine by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 29. Methylphenidate: Calcium carbonate reduces the effects of methylphenidate by altering GI absorption. For extended-release capsules (e.g., Ritalin LA), co-administration with antacids or acid suppressants may alter drug release. Consider separating administration. Monitor closely. 30. Metoprolol: Calcium carbonate decreases the effects and levels of metoprolol by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Separate administration by 2 hours. Use caution and monitor closely. 31. Mexiletine: Calcium carbonate increases the levels or effects of mexiletine by enhancing passive renal tubular reabsorption in a basic urine environment. Use caution and monitor closely. 32. Moxifloxacin: Calcium carbonate and moxifloxacin can mutually decrease each other's levels by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Separate administration by 2 hours. Use caution and monitor closely. 33. Mycophenolate: Calcium carbonate decreases the levels or effects of mycophenolate by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 34. Nadolol: Calcium carbonate decreases the effects and levels of nadolol by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Separate administration by 2 hours. Use caution and monitor closely. 35. Nebivolol: Calcium carbonate decreases the effects and levels of nebivolol by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Separate administration by 2 hours. Use caution and monitor closely. 36. Neratinib: Calcium carbonate decreases the levels or effects of neratinib by increasing gastric pH. Separate antacid and neratinib dosing by 3 hours. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 37. Nilotinib: Calcium carbonate decreases the levels of nilotinib by increasing gastric pH. Avoid this interaction by administering antacids 2 hours before or after nilotinib. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 38. Nitrofurantoin: Calcium carbonate decreases the levels of nitrofurantoin by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Separate administration by 2 hours. Use caution and monitor closely. 39. Omadacycline: Calcium carbonate decreases the levels or effects of omadacycline by inhibiting GI absorption. Multivalent cation-containing products may impair absorption of tetracyclines. Separate dosing of tetracyclines from these products. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 40. Paloparateriparatide: Drugs affecting serum calcium may alter the therapeutic response of paloparateriparatide. Measure serum calcium more frequently if co-administered, especially after initiating, discontinuing, or adjusting doses. Use caution and monitor closely. 41. Pamidronate: Calcium carbonate decreases the levels of pamidronate by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Separate administration by 30 minutes. Use caution and monitor closely. 42. Pancrelipase: Calcium carbonate reduces the effects of pancrelipase through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Antacids may negate the beneficial effects of enzymes. Use caution and monitor closely. 43. Penbutolol: Calcium carbonate decreases the effects and levels of penbutolol by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Separate administration by 2 hours. Use caution and monitor closely. 44. Penicillamine: Calcium carbonate decreases the levels of penicillamine by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Separate administration by 2 hours. Use caution and monitor closely. 45. Perindopril: Calcium carbonate reduces the effects of perindopril through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. 46. Pexidartinib: Calcium carbonate decreases the levels or effects of pexidartinib by inhibiting GI absorption. Separate pexidartinib by 2 hours before or after taking a locally-acting antacid. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 47. Pindolol: Calcium carbonate decreases the effects and levels of pindolol by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Separate administration by 2 hours. Use caution and monitor closely. 48. Polysaccharide Iron: Calcium carbonate decreases the levels or effects of polysaccharide iron by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 49. Posaconazole: Calcium carbonate decreases the levels or effects of posaconazole by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 50. Potassium Phosphates (IV): Calcium carbonate decreases the effects of potassium phosphates by cation binding in the GI tract. Calcium also decreases serum phosphate concentration by binding dietary phosphate. Use alternatives if available. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 51. Propranolol: Calcium carbonate decreases the effects and levels of propranolol by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Separate administration by 2 hours. Use caution and monitor closely. 52. Quinapril: Calcium carbonate reduces the effects of quinapril through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. 53. Quinidine: Calcium carbonate increases the levels or effects of quinidine by enhancing passive renal tubular reabsorption in a basic urine environment. Elevated quinidine plasma levels, potentially causing cardiac conduction disturbances and arrhythmias, may occur. Use caution and monitor closely. 54. Ramipril: Calcium carbonate reduces the effects of ramipril through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor closely. 55. Rifampin: Concomitant antacid administration may reduce the absorption of rifampin. Daily doses of rifampin should be given at least 1 hour before ingestion of antacids. Use caution and monitor closely. 56. Rilpivirine: Calcium carbonate decreases the levels of rilpivirine by increasing gastric pH. Co-administration of antacids with rilpivirine may cause significant decreases in rilpivirine plasma concentrations. If antacids must be administered, they should be given at least 2 hours before or at least 4 hours after rilpivirine. For the combination product dolutegravir/rilpivirine, antacids should be given at least 4 hours before or at least 6 hours afterwards. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 57. Riociguat: Calcium carbonate decreases the levels of riociguat by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Separate administration by at least 1 hour. Use caution and monitor closely. 58. Risedronate: Calcium carbonate decreases the levels of risedronate by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Separate administration by 30 minutes. Use caution and monitor closely. 59. Rose Hips: Calcium carbonate decreases the levels or effects of rose hips by increasing gastric pH. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor closely. 60. Rosuvastatin: Calcium carbonate decreases the levels of rosuvastatin by inhibiting GI absorption. This interaction applies only to oral forms of both agents. Separate administration by 2 hours. Use caution and monitor closely. 61. Sarecycline: Calcium carbonate decreases the levels or effects of sarecycline by inhibiting GI absorption. Multivalent cation-containing products may impair absorption of tetracyclines. Separate dosing of tetracyclines from these products. Modify therapy and monitor closely.
